themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 114 THIS WEEK, a 274% spike versus the 8-week baseline of 30.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.93), signaling rapid deterioration of roads and sidewalks across the Upper West Side that may require immediate DOT intervention.
evidence: 114 street condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 30.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.93 indicates statistically severe anomaly
reporting_angles: Investigate which specific streets or neighborhoods are seeing the worst deterioration; map the complaints geographically
Contact DOT to understand why this spike occurred this week—weather event, deferred maintenance, or seasonal pattern?

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK versus a 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16), suggesting either a new retail opening or enforcement gap in unlicensed dispensaries on the Upper West Side.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.16 indicates highly significant spike
reporting_angles: Identify which specific cannabis retailers (licensed or unlicensed) are subject of complaints; verify licensing status with state cannabis control board
Interview community members and local business owners about what sparked complaints this week—odor, customer conduct, lack of signage, or location near schools/parks?

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Reports Surge
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints hit 3 THIS WEEK, a 700% spike from the 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.77), suggesting a potential environmental contamination event or pattern requiring DSNY and DOHMH coordination.
evidence: 3 hazardous materials complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.77 indicates severe statistical anomaly
reporting_angles: Obtain detailed 311 complaint descriptions to identify what materials were reported and where; cross-reference with DOB permits to determine if construction or demolition is releasing contaminants
Contact DOHMH and DSNY to determine if they've issued advisories or conducted site investigations in response to this week's spike

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 68 LAST WEEK, a 256% spike versus the 8-week average of 19.1 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.04), pointing to construction activity, street fairs, or traffic congestion affecting residents.
evidence: 68 street/sidewalk noise complaints filed last week vs. 19.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.04 indicates statistically severe spike
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify hotspot blocks or corridors; determine if complaints cluster around specific construction sites, street vending areas, or transit hubs
Interview NYPD and NYC Parks to understand if permitted street events or construction projects were active last week

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Rising
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints reached 66 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 59% increase from the 8-week average of 41.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 3.76), reflecting potential garbage accumulation, rodent activity, or public space degradation across the district.
evidence: 66 unsanitary condition complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 41.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with Community Board's repeated budget request for expanded code enforcement
reporting_angles: Determine if spike is tied to specific DSNY service gaps, holiday schedules, or refuse management issues; cross-check with DSNY schedules
Interview residents and small business owners in the district about the visible cleanliness situation and whether complaints reflect perception or real deterioration
